summary: Pan-fried potato gnocchi with radicchio, leeks and ricotta salata: russets baked 45 minutes on a bed of kosher salt, riced, mixed with flour, egg and milk into a soft, not sticky dough, shaped, boiled until they float plus 30 seconds, then pan-fried crispy with leeks and radicchio; serves 6.
glance: 2 pounds russets, baked at 450°F on a layer of kosher salt for about 45 minutes
2 1/2 cups flour, 2 eggs, 1/2 cup milk, nutmeg
until they float, then another 30 seconds; toss with oil
faq: Why bake the potatoes on salt?
It lets heat and air circulate under the potato and dries up any moisture that seeps out. Moist potatoes are the enemy of gnocchi, so cut them in half while they cool to let more steam escape.
Why add egg to gnocchi?
Not everyone does, but a small amount adds a little insurance against the dumplings falling apart, and a pleasing flavor.
What tool should I use to mash the potatoes?
A potato ricer is ideal: it takes them apart into a fluffy pile without breaking up the starch granules into a sticky mass. A food mill or box grater also work.
How much flour do I need?

The critical factor: the dough should stick together but not be sticky, so the gnocchi neither fall apart nor have a leaden texture. Until you get the hang of it, boil a test gnocchi or two; they only take a couple of minutes.
How do I shape the grooves?

The traditional tool is a fork, but the author prefers a cheap gnocchi board, which is faster and makes neater, deeper grooves: roll each piece while pressing in with your thumb to create an indentation.
Why pan-fry gnocchi?
Pan-frying the boiled gnocchi adds crispy textural contrast to the creamy interior and toasty flavor notes. Boiled gnocchi can be oiled, cooled and refrigerated ahead.

summary: Braised fennel: fennel halves seared cut-side down about 5 minutes in olive oil, then braised covered 10-20 minutes on a bed of garlic, onion and carrot with orange juice and zest, dry vermouth and water until tender, finished with olive oil, flaky salt, fronds and optional fennel pollen; serves 4 as a side.
glance: covered on low heat, 10 to 20 minutes depending on bulb size
zest and juice of 1 mandarin, 1/4 cup dry vermouth, 1/2 cup water
a Dutch oven big enough to hold the fennel in a single layer
faq: What is a proper braise?

Sear the heck out of your main ingredient to develop browned flavors, remove it, quickly sweat the other vegetables, then return the main ingredient with a small amount of flavorful liquid. With the lid on and heat lowered, everything steams until tender while the flavors marry and the sauce emulsifies into silky goodness.
Why omit celery from the mirepoix?
The usual mirepoix is carrots, onions and celery, but celery might muddy the flavor of the fennel.
Why vermouth and orange?

Dry vermouth for its complex aromatics, and orange juice (augmented with zest) because it pairs beautifully with fennel. A chef friend suggested star anise to emphasize fennel's licorice notes, which the author hasn't tried.
What is fennel pollen?
Pretty amazing stuff with an aroma like summer in Provence in a jar. It's rather expensive but a pinch goes a long way; the dish is fine without it.
How do I know the fennel is done?
When it is completely tender when probed with a knife. Adjust the heat to keep a steady amount of steam without boiling off all the liquid, adding a bit more if needed.

summary: Eggplant parmigiana for late summer: peeled eggplant planks salted and drained at least 30 minutes, dredged in flour, egg and panko and fried until brown, layered three times with tomato sauce, mozzarella, Parmigiano and basil, baked 20 minutes at 400°F and topped with diced fresh heirloom tomatoes; serves 6.
glance: 3 large or 5 smaller globe, about 4 pounds, sliced scant 1/2 inch thick, salted at least 30 minutes
1/4 inch of vegetable oil, about 2 minutes per side
400°F for about 20 minutes, just to melt the cheese
faq: Why salt and drain the eggplant here?

The author doesn't bother for most dishes, but here it makes a big difference: you don't want liquid coming off the eggplant in the oven making the breading soggy. Layer with kosher salt in a colander, weight with a plate and cans, and drain at least 30 minutes, then wipe off excess salt.
How do I choose eggplant?
Look for very dense ones: when you pick one up, you should be surprised at how heavy it is.
Why panko?
Japanese panko breadcrumbs fry up so light and crispy; find them at Asian grocery stores and better mainstream markets.
Why add fresh tomatoes at the end?

Canned tomatoes make the sauce, and a dice of fresh heirloom cherry tomatoes and basil goes on top after baking: the combination of fresh and cooked tomato flavor is unbeatable. Don't add salt to the sauce because the eggplant retains residual salt.
How do I fry the eggplant?

Use vegetable oil (not olive oil, which smokes) about 1/4 inch deep on high heat, dredge in flour, egg and panko, fry until brown on both sides, about 2 minutes each; they should be tender at this point since baking only melts the cheese.

summary: Grilled eggplant and shiitake bruschetta with a red wine, tamari and miso glaze reduced until syrupy: Japanese eggplant and shiitake caps grilled until tender, glazed, and piled on oiled grilled country bread with parsley, sea salt and parmesan; makes 4 pieces, from a self-described failed experiment.
glance: 1/2 cup red wine, 1/4 cup tamari, 2 tablespoons brown miso, mirin and shiitake stems, simmered until syrupy
eggplant longer than shiitake; glaze the eggplant for the last few minutes
Vegetarian; vegan if you omit the parmesan; gluten-free if you omit the bread
faq: What was the failed experiment?

The author wanted to glaze a plate with sauce in the microwave (20 seconds at a time until it barely dries into a thick coating) so diners could swab the reduced sauce with moist food and rehydrate the flavors. It made an ugly brown splotchy mess, so he brushed the reduced glaze across the plate instead.
How do I make the glaze?
Combine the red wine (a Tempranillo), tamari, brown miso, mirin (or sugar) and shiitake stems in a small saucepan, boil, then simmer until syrupy on a spoon after cooling a second; remove the stems.
How do I grill the vegetables?

Rub the Japanese eggplant (quartered lengthwise) and shiitake caps with neutral oil and salt and cook on a grill pan or charcoal grill until tender, flipping each item only once for intact grill marks. Glaze the eggplant for the last few minutes.
How do I grill the bread?
Rub olive oil on both sides of the country bread and grill until lightly brown, watching closely so it doesn't char.
How do I serve it?

Brush a line of the remaining sauce down a long platter (or on individual plates), pile eggplant and shiitake on each slice, and top with parsley, sea salt, black pepper and slivers of parmesan. A fine first course for dinner on the deck.

summary: Braised Belgian endive with sauce gribiche: endive halves browned 3 minutes cut-side down and braised covered about 10 minutes with 1/4 cup water, cooled, and served with a classic mustardy sauce of sieved hard-boiled yolk, olive oil, vinegar, cornichons, capers, chervil or parsley and tarragon; serves 4 in 30 minutes.
glance: 30 minutes if you have a hard-boiled egg
8 Belgian endives, halved lengthwise with the stem end intact
1 hard-boiled egg, Dijon, 1/4 cup olive oil, vinegar, cornichons, capers, herbs
faq: What is sauce gribiche?

A classic French sauce powerfully flavored with mustard, vinegar, cornichons, capers and a lot of fresh herbs. The author first tasted it as an intern at Seattle's Canlis, where Chef Franey serves it with asparagus; he likes it equally with braised Belgian endive or steamed artichoke hearts.
How is the sauce made?

Similar to homemade mayonnaise: separate the hard-boiled egg, finely dice the white, force the yolk through a fine sieve, whisk with Dijon into a paste, slowly drizzle in the olive oil, then mix in the vinegar, cornichons, capers, herbs and egg white. It doesn't need a perfect emulsion; partial separation is fine.
Why not trim the endive stem end?
Don't trim the stem end or the endives will fall apart; cook them cut-side down in oil with a big pinch of salt until beginning to brown, about 3 minutes.
Can I serve the endive without the sauce?
Yes; try something flavorful such as fresh-squeezed orange juice in place of the water for the braising liquid.
Is it served hot or cold?
Set the braised endive aside to cool to room temperature (or refrigerate) and serve chilled or at room temperature with the sauce spooned over, and good bread to mop up the extras.

summary: Vegetarian nuoc cham, the Vietnamese dipping sauce made without fish sauce: water, sugar and a small piece of kombu steeped 10 minutes, then mixed with lime juice, garlic, chiles, a little soy sauce and salt for savory, salty, sweet, spicy and sour balance; makes 1 cup in 10 minutes.
glance: a small piece of dried kombu steeped 10 minutes plus 1 tablespoon soy sauce
a few days in the refrigerator
Vegan; gluten-free option (omit or check the soy sauce)
faq: What is nuoc cham?
The quintessential Vietnamese dipping sauce: fish sauce seasoned with sugar, lime juice, garlic and chiles.
How does this version get umami without fish sauce?

A little bit of kombu and soy sauce infuse the oceanic umami flavor that would otherwise be missing. Bring the water, sugar and kombu to a simmer, turn off the heat, stand ten minutes, then remove the kombu.
How should it taste?
A balance of savory, salty, sweet, spicy and sour; taste and adjust the seasoning after mixing in the lime juice, garlic, chiles, soy sauce, salt and optional julienned carrots.
What do I serve it with?
Banh xeo, or as an alternative to the ginger-grapefruit sauce in rice vermicelli (bun).
How long does it keep?
Serve immediately or keep in the refrigerator for a few days.

summary: Rice vermicelli bun with ginger-grapefruit sauce, from the Herbivoracious cookbook: noodles soaked in hot water, topped with caramelized sweet-soy tofu, fried shallots, pickled carrot and daikon, mango, cucumber, herbs and a vegetarian sauce of grapefruit and lime juice; vegan, serves 4 in 45 minutes.
glance: 8 ounces Vietnamese rice vermicelli, soaked 10 minutes in hot water off the heat
grapefruit and lime juice, sugar, ginger, soy sauce, salt, strongly flavored
faq: What is bun?

Pronounced roughly "boon": thin Vietnamese rice noodles topped with a variety of cooked and fresh ingredients, lots of herbs and a sweet-and-savory sauce, a light, healthy meal-in-a-bowl that is salad and entree in one.
What is the key to bun?

The mise en place: you have quite a few ingredients to prepare, nothing complicated, but you want to be organized for final assembly. Remember to grate the zest from one of the limes before juicing them.
How do I cook the noodles?
Boil water, remove it from the heat, add the rice noodles and let sit ten minutes; they should be tender but definitely not mushy. Drain and reserve.
How do I make the sauce vegetarian?

Instead of fish sauce, combine the juice from cutting grapefruit supremes and squeezing the leftover pieces with lime juice, sugar, ginger, soy sauce and salt. It must be strongly flavored to play off the other ingredients.
Do I need a mandoline?

Not strictly, but the author calls it one of the best tools for streamlining prep: the simple $20 Benriner is what most chefs use, making quick work of uniform slices and juliennes for the carrot and daikon.

summary: Reconstructed tarte tatin with spun sugar: apples roasted in light caramel in a skillet at 400°F while a 10-inch puff pastry circle bakes separately so it stays crunchy, then the apples are arranged in the pastry's cut-out center, glazed with jam and topped with fork-spun caramel; serves 4.
glance: 400°F: apples until tender, a 10-inch puff pastry circle until golden brown (different times)
3 baking apples, peeled, cored and sliced medium
2/3 cup sugar for the apples; remaining sugar melted into a medium caramel for spun sugar
faq: What is the main idea?

Cook the crust separately from the apples and caramel so it remains crunchy. The method is based partly on one by Dieter Schoemer in Culinary Artistry. A normal flaky pie crust can replace the puff pastry.
How do I assemble it?

Cut a rim about 3/4 inch in from the edge of the baked pastry circle with a paring knife (without removing any pastry) so the center drops to form a dish, lay the apples in concentric rings tucked under the edge, glaze with warmed jam, and pour over the leftover apple juices and caramel, reducing if needed.
How do I make spun sugar?

Dip the tines of a fork in the medium caramel and pull vertically; at the right temperature it forms a thin strand, which you carefully stretch with your fingers and lay over the tart. The author didn't need the more technical methods with water, corn syrup or cream of tartar.
Is caramel dangerous?
Be careful: caramel will burn you very easily.
Can I make individual portions?
Yes, the author thinks individual portions would be quite striking. A splash of Calvados is optional.

summary: Crispy polenta cakes with white beans and morels in half an hour: leftover chilled polenta formed into 3/8-inch patties and fried until quite golden and crispy, served on cannellini simmered with rehydrated dried morels, rosemary and mushroom broth; vegan, serves 4.
glance: about half an hour with leftover polenta
6 cups cooked and chilled, or 2 cups dry coarse cornmeal cooked about 30 minutes and chilled at least 3 hours
1/4 cup olive oil, until quite golden-brown on both sides
faq: What polenta works?

Leftover polenta, including with cheese or other flavorings, as long as it has set firm enough to form a patty. If you don't have any, make a fresh batch at lunchtime that will be firm for dinner, needing only salt.
What is the key to crispy cakes?
Be bold and really fry the cakes until quite crispy and brown on the outside: the contrast of the crust with the soft interior is wonderful.
How do I prepare the morels?

Cover 16 dried morels with boiling water for 15 minutes, drain and reserve the soaking liquid strained through a fine sieve, halve any larger than bite-sized, fry 2 minutes with salt and rosemary, then add the beans and 1/2 cup of soaking liquid and simmer.
How do I shape the cakes?
Form 1/2 cup of chilled polenta into a patty about 3/8 inch thick; make 8 patties and fry in two batches in a large skillet, preferably cast iron, over medium-high heat.
What goes with them?
The author says they're especially good with red wine braised cabbage.

summary: Alioli, garlicky Spanish mayonnaise: a paste of 4 cloves of garlic whizzed in a blender with egg yolks, lemon juice or sherry vinegar and salt, then 1 cup of olive oil drizzled in to emulsify; makes 1.5 cups in a few minutes, served with boiled potatoes smashed lightly on the plate.
glance: 4 cloves garlic, 2 egg yolks, 1.5 tablespoons lemon juice or sherry vinegar, 1 cup olive oil
up to a day refrigerated; the garlic flavor becomes more intense but rounded
Vegetarian and gluten-free; not vegan; contains raw egg
faq: What is alioli?

A close Spanish cousin of French aioli: a simple home-made mayonnaise that comes together in a few minutes, very garlicky. Serve with any raw or cooked vegetable, or a slab of cold tortilla (Spanish frittata) on crusty bread, and famously with potatoes.
How do I make it?

Mince the garlic to a fine paste and whiz in a blender with the egg yolks, lemon juice and 1.5 teaspoons of salt for a minute, then remove the little cap in the top and slowly drizzle in the olive oil to emulsify. It's working when it turns thick and opaque.
Is it safe to eat raw eggs?

Like any homemade mayonnaise it uses raw eggs, so use your own judgment. Pasteurized whole eggs may be available, which would be safer. The author wouldn't serve it to the very young or old or anyone with a compromised immune system.
How do I serve it with potatoes?
The author boiled potatoes in their jackets; guests smash a potato lightly on the plate and drizzle on some sauce.
Can I make it ahead?
Yes, at the last minute or up to a day in advance, refrigerated; the garlic flavor becomes even more intense but rounded overnight.
